title: This Time It’s Personal: How Behavioral Science Proved What One Business Leader Saw in 1993
gist: BCG Henderson Institute argues that 75% of corporate change programs fail because change is behavioral, as Jeanie Duck claimed in 1993, and that later behavioral science (narrative recall, endowed progress effect, IKEA effect) now validates her intuition. It offers practical techniques for storytelling, momentum and employee agency, illustrated by Ford, Aetna and Ericsson.

insights.claim: BCG's latest research finds that 75% of corporate change programs fail, a failure rate that has persisted since 1993.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Base rate for transformation stories: most announced restructurings and turnarounds should be discounted until execution evidence appears.
insights.quote: Yet corporate change programs have continued to fail at astonishingly high rates—75%, according to our latest research.

insights.claim: Jeanie Duck argued in a 1993 Harvard Business Review article that the root cause of most change failures is behavioral rather than strategic, financial, or operational.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: When evaluating a turnaround, assess management's people/behavior execution capability, not just the strategic plan.
insights.quote: the root cause of most change failures wasn’t strategic, financial, or operational—it was behavioral.

insights.claim: Duck's behavioral insight failed to change practice for decades because the behavioral-science evidence to confirm it did not yet exist in 1993; BCG argues the accumulated science now vindicates it.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Practitioner frameworks gain adoption only when backed by evidence; expect consulting demand for 'science-based' change programs.
insights.quote: Duck’s insight, powerful though it was, arrived ahead of its time.
insights.locator: Why did that record of failure continue?

insights.claim: BCG is packaging its behavioral change approach into a book, How Change Really Works, with seven science-based principles, positioning it as the first truly human-centered change program.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Signals BCG's commercial push into behavior-led transformation consulting.
insights.quote: seven principles that give leaders, for the first time, a truly human-centered program that can deliver lasting change

insights.claim: A 1999 study by Karen Zabrucky and DeWayne Moore with 40 adults found narrative passages were read faster, had more inconsistencies detected, and were better remembered than equally complex expository essays.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Narrative-led management communication is more likely to be absorbed than detailed information dumps.
insights.quote: Narrative passages thus appear to be less demanding of effective regulation skills than expository passages.

insights.claim: Distributing information, such as sending a detailed binder to managers, is insufficient for change; messages must be communicated intentionally, strategically, and repeatedly.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Watch whether leadership repeats a consistent narrative, not just publishes plans.
insights.quote: it wasn’t enough to distribute information—such as by sending a detailed binder to managers
insights.locator: Jeanie Duck recognized the critical role

insights.claim: BCG identifies three effective change-story types: the threat story (change or die), the fitness story (change makes us stronger), and the destiny story (change realizes full potential).
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: A lens for reading CEO letters and turnaround messaging.
insights.locator: In our own experiences leading change programs

insights.claim: Ford CEO Alan Mulally's 2006 company-wide 'threat story' email preceded a return to profitability in under three years without a government bailout.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Clear, candid CEO communication of competitive threat can be a leading indicator of turnaround execution.
insights.quote: But pockets of success aren’t enough. Not today. Not in this competitive environment.

insights.claim: Employees believe in a change initiative only after seeing modeled behavior, tangible action, and visible results, not because leadership asks them to.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Early visible wins matter more than announcements in judging whether a transformation will stick.
insights.quote: They believe because they’re actually seeing behavior, action, and results that lead them to conclude that the program works.

insights.claim: In Nunes and Dreze's 2006 endowed-progress experiment with 300 car-wash customers, cards giving two free stamps toward ten purchases achieved a 34% redemption rate versus 19% for an equivalent eight-purchase card with no head start.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Perceived head starts materially lift completion—relevant to loyalty programs, onboarding and transformation design.
insights.quote: the redemption rate for the group with the perceived head start was 34%, significantly higher than the 19% redemption rate
insights.locator: In 2006, this insight found scientific support

insights.claim: BCG recommends four momentum techniques: show belief publicly, promote wins, set new challenges for overperforming teams, and engineer fresh starts for underperforming teams.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Checklist for evaluating how management sustains a multi-year transformation.
insights.locator: In our own practice, we have observed four

insights.claim: Aetna COO Katerina Guerraz sustained a post-pandemic change program via a 90-day plan, a twice-monthly 'transformation email', and team success stories at town halls, creating a virtuous cycle of momentum.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Structured internal win-promotion is an observable signal of transformation discipline.
insights.locator: The leaders of Aetna, the US insurer

insights.claim: In Michael Norton's IKEA-effect experiment, students who assembled IKEA boxes were willing to pay 63% more for them than students who inspected identical preassembled boxes.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Effort-based ownership raises perceived value—supports co-creation in products and in change programs.
insights.quote: Putting effort into something makes you value it.

insights.claim: Transformations are more likely to succeed when employees feel their own thumbprints are on the design; BCG proposes tiered experiences of decision making, influence, and representation to create this ownership.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Broad employee participation is a predictor of transformation success worth probing in management access.
insights.quote: transformations are more likely to succeed when employees feel that their own thumbprints are on the design
insights.locator: In our own practice, we have observed that transformations

insights.claim: Ericsson drove adoption of a new digital sales platform by giving regional cross-functional teams co-ownership and charging benefiting business units a small symbolic fee, on the logic that free tools lack adoption incentives.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Internal charge-backs can be a deliberate adoption lever, not just cost allocation—relevant to enterprise digital/AI rollouts.
insights.quote: If you bring in something new and it’s free for all, then there’s no incentive to really adopt it or make it work.

insights.claim: The article's section heading dates the agency science to 2012 while the body dates the IKEA-effect confirmation to 2022, an internal inconsistency in the cited timeline.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/julia-dhar
insights.so_what: Minor sourcing caveat when citing the IKEA-effect date from this piece.
insights.quote: In 2022, Duck’s practical insight received scientific confirmation with the discovery of the IKEA effect.
